Measured progress and public evidence

The research team published its measurements on Wednesday. The study compares energy use across three public buildings and explains how the instruments were calibrated. Residents can inspect the method and the complete findings.

Electricity use fell by twelve percent during the measured period. The result does not establish that the same saving will occur in every building. The authors describe weather and occupancy as important sources of uncertainty.

A council engineer said that maintenance, rather than new equipment, explained much of the change. Independent reviewers will repeat the work next year before the council makes a larger investment.
